title: File:Allegory of Emperor Charles V as Ruler of the World (by Peter Paul Rubens) - Residenzgalerie, Salzburg.jpg
description:
Rubens was distinguished by his success as an artist and his skill as a diplomat. In 1624 the Spanish King Philip IV (1605–1665) raised him to the nobility.
In 1603/04, as court painter to Duke Vincenzo Gonzaga II (1594–1627), he travelled to Spain on a diplomatic mission. Here he encountered the powerful dynasty of the Habsburg rulers, whose display of splendour emulated that of Charles V (1500–1558), and studied the emperor portraits of Titian (1477–1576). On his return to Mantua, he made a copy of a painting by Parmigianino (1503–1540) belonging to the Duke – the "Allegory of Charles V as Ruler of the World". Charles’s status as supreme military commander is shown by the shining armour with white heightening and by the sword in his left hand. The insignia of his office, crown and sceptre, are further symbols of his power. The cape he wears over his armour is set with pearls and precious stones, completing the imposing imperial figure. On a red ribbon around his neck is the Order of the Golden Fleece, of which as sovereign he is the Grand Master. A genius holding a globe symbolises the emperor’s wide-ranging dominion.

description: One of the three images depicted in Peter Paul Reuban's Decent from the Cross, a triptych of paintings featuring Christ's crucifixion. The paintings still hang in their original location the Cathedral of Our Lady in Antwerp, Belgium. The Arrases visited Belgium during their 1913 tour of Europe. Edmund F. Arras (7/7/1875-10/19/1951), a prominent Columbus businessman and entrepreneur, founded one of Columbus, Ohio’s first property rental agencies in 1892. Trained as a lawyer, he graduated from OSU law school in 1896 and went on to hold positions in numerous civic groups around the city. He was particularly active within Kiwanis International and was involved with several local religious organizations. In 1913, he and his wife Elizabeth traveled to the World Sunday School Association Convention in Zurich, Switzerland. They continued on to travel extensively throughout Europe documenting their journey through photographs. Due to the timing of their trip, these photos comprise a valuable collection of images of European cities later devastated by war. The Arras family’s lantern slides and negatives include images from their 1913 travels through US east coast cities, Atlantic islands of the Azores, Madeira, Gibraltar and the countries of Algeria, Italy, Switzerland, Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, France, England, and Ireland. Also included are images from their 1920 train journey from Chicago to the western US for the Kiwanis Convention in Portland. These photographs include images of Chicago, Denver and western National Parks.
